If the knights of ren decided to turn against the first order as a third party, would it be in character, and a clever move, for Hux to disguise a thermal detonator as a holocron, and putting it on

message.content: Yes, in a limited sense, it would be in character for Hux to try to exploit the Knights of Ren’s Jedi fixation, because he is politically opportunistic and willing to use whatever symbolic or military advantage can remove a rival. If the Knights of Ren became a separate force, Hux would see them not as allies but as dangerous traitors with a symbolic claim to the Order. He is the kind of character who would try to turn their obsession against them, especially if it could make him look like the rational authority of the First Order. However, disguising a thermal detonator as a holocron would be cleverer than strictly in character, because Hux is more a military bureaucrat and power-seeker than a patient Jedi historian. The idea works dramatically: it plays on Kylo Ren’s need for Jedi legitimacy and could make the Knights reach for or approach something they believe is sacred. But Hux would probably not personally craft the disguise, nor would he choose the most elegant trap available. He would more likely order a deception, set up a meeting, or hide explosives in a room rather than make an artifact-level con. It would be most plausible if the detonator was not merely “a thermal detonator made to look like a holocron,” but part of a larger Hux-style trap: a false Jedi relic, a fake surrender, or a “safe” location where the Knights could be killed while he claimed to be restoring order. That version fits him better. Hux’s cruelty is usually institutional, public, and status-driven. A fake holocron could be his bait, but the real murder would probably come from stormtroopers, a force pike ambush, or a staged betrayal. The detonator itself would be the payoff, not the proof of his cleverness. So the move is a good one-time scheme, but it is not a fully canonical Hux signature; it is a clever twist that would work best if it is an improvised, desperate, or politically necessary trick. If Hux had no other option, or if he truly believed he could use the Jedi mythos to crush Kylo Ren’s faction, the plan makes sense. But as a recurring or defining trait, it is too subtle and too lore-specific for Hux. The cleaner character match is: Hux would use the holocron as bait, not as his personal masterpiece.
